 The Altruists: Netflix’s gripping true crime drama charts the rise and fall of a crypto empire
 Entertainment 
 By Kayleigh Dray 
 6 November Credit: Netflix
 Credit: Netflix
 4 min read
 save for later
 Make us preferred on Google
 Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle take on the “greatest financial fraud ever perpetrated” in The Altruists , aka your next must-watch series.
 Is there anything better than a juicy true crime ? Not the kind that dusts off a murder case or brutal assault; I’m talking about the kind of stranger-than-fiction drama that delves deep into an unbelievable con, scam or heist – the sort that makes us binge an entire series in one big greedy gulp. The kind that has us talking about what we’ve just witnessed. The kind with actors who are giving Emmy energy from the get-go. Enter stage left, then, The Altruists , starring Shardlake ’s Anthony Boyle and the inimitable Julia Garner (of Ozark and Weapons fame).
 Inspired by New York magazine’s reporting on the spectacular collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison’s cryptocurrency exchange and hedge fund, FTX, the series takes us inside a story that is almost too extraordinary to be true. We’re talking dizzying sums of money, eye-watering ambition and a financial empire that went from being valued in the billions to spectacularly imploding – with two very complicated people at its centre.
 Still, while the headlines have already given us the jaw-dropping numbers and the courtroom drama, The Altruists is interested in something rather more intimate: the people behind the scandal. What makes two seemingly brilliant young minds build something so enormous, and what happens when the world they’ve created begins to crumble around them?

 As creator Graham Moore told Netflix’s Tudum , he was fascinated by Bankman-Fried and Ellison from the outset. In fact, he admits: “I’m not nearly a good enough writer to create characters as fascinating as either Sam Bankman-Fried or Caroline Ellison.”
 Rather than simply recreate the scandal we’ve all read about, Moore wanted to get under the skin of the people involved – and explore the moments the public never got to see. “[We didn’t want to create a] kind of headline Wikipedia version of the story, but to tell what we believed was the much more fascinating, intimate, personal, deeply heartbreaking story of these two people,” he says – and that meant making a very deliberate creative choice. 
 “If a moment already existed on film somewhere, we weren’t going to show it. We were only going to show you things that by definition couldn’t have been filmed before.” In other words, forget another straightforward retelling of the headlines; this is a chance to get closer than ever to the people behind one of the most astonishing financial scandals of our time.
 It was the ‘greatest financial fraud ever perpetrated’ in the USA What is the true story behind The Altruists ?
 Caroline Ellison was a maths whizz who graduated from Stanford University and found herself running Alameda Research (aka the cryptocurrency trading firm closely tied to FTX) at the tender age of 28. Its founder? Sam Bankman-Fried, the eccentric billionaire who had become the poster boy for a new generation of tech entrepreneurs… and Caroline’s on-again, off-again boyfriend.
 The pair had met while working at quantitative trading firm Jane Street before Bankman-Fried recruited Ellison to join Alameda. As their professional lives became increasingly intertwined, so did their personal ones. And, behind the headlines about their seemingly unstoppable success, FTX (attracting billions in investment and building a reputation as one of the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchanges) began funnelling money into Alameda to cover trading losses and risky bets. 
 When FTX began to collapse in November 2022, the scale of the financial hole was staggering. Ellison pleaded guilty to fraud and conspiracy charges, and became a key witness against her former partner, testifying that Bankman-Fried had directed her to commit crimes. He was subsequently convicted and sentenced to 25 years in prison. 
 Ellison, meanwhile, was praised for her cooperation with prosecutors and sentenced to two years for her role in what US District Judge Lewis A Kaplan declared the “greatest financial fraud ever perpetrated in this country”. 
 Credit: RICARDO HUBBS/NETFLIX
 Ellison was released from federal custody in January 2026, after serving around 14 months, and has since embarked on a rather unexpected new chapter. In September, it emerged that she had joined Manifund, a philanthropic funding platform, where she is now working on its technology and how charitable money is distributed. 
 The company’s co-founder Austin Chen defended the decision to hire her, saying: “I believe in redemption. Caroline has admitted her faults, worked to make creditors whole and served her time in prison.” Ellison herself said she was grateful for the opportunity to be judged on her current work rather than her past.
 It’s a fascinating, and certainly controversial, postscript to a story that already has more twists than most fictional dramas. And if that doesn’t make you curious to see Julia Garner take on Caroline Ellison, I’m not sure what will.
 All eight episodes of The Altruists are scheduled to premiere on Netflix on 19 November.
